note: Track range (voice-breath-range), step 3: a few notes lower (voice-hill low, a semitone lower each hold), a few notes higher (voice-hill high, light), then a five-note run that climbs a semitone each pass up to the edge of the range. The five-note runs in the book are all Medium, so the run is picked as medium, not hard.

exercise.title: A few notes lower, a few notes higher
exercise.why: Your range grows from its edges, a semitone at a time and only while the sound stays easy, so each block starts inside your range and moves one small step past it.

cells.heading: Lower, a semitone at a time

cells.text:
Press Start below: a note plays first, then the mic starts. Hold that note on "oo": the ball rolls down into the hollow as your voice goes low, and the ring fills while you stay there. Each hold is a semitone lower, and the new note plays in the breath between.
Keep it quiet: a low note pushed for volume goes flat.

Press Start below: a note plays first, then the mic starts. Hold a light sound on "oo" in head voice: the ball climbs to the top as your voice goes up, and the ring fills while you stay there.
_Don't reach for high notes: keep the high holds quiet, and stop if your throat tightens._

Press Play below to hear the run: the mic starts with it. The run goes from Do up to Sol and back, and each pass starts a semitone higher. Sing it lightly on "ah", and move to "oo" when a pass feels tight.
Stop at the pass that no longer feels easy. That pass is the edge of your range today, and the edge moves up a little at a time.
